title: Optimal route & fallback matrix for staged deployments
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create a canonical routing and fallback matrix that unambiguously defines how requests are routed when model version pinning, region preferences, customer tier restrictions, and staged rollouts (canary / A-B) interact. The matrix should be implementable by the routing-resolver service and cover sticky affinity, short-lived consistency for canary cohorts, and graceful degrade paths to fewer-capable variants when capacity or latency SLOs are violated.
background: We have multiple overlapping policies that influence final route selection: explicit model pins, rollout assignment percentages, region affinity, tenant tier (hosted vs dedicated), and variant fallbacks (quantized/latency-optimized variants). Past incidents showed ambiguous resolution order caused canary cohorts to be bounced to incompatible variants or wrong regions under capacity pressure. This ticket defines a deterministic, testable matrix and a small set of runtime rules to avoid regressions.
design_decisions: 1) Resolve explicit model pin first: if a request includes a user-specified model_version, we honor it if available in the selected region/tier; otherwise consult fallback chain. 2) Next apply tier constraints: tenant subscription tier filters candidate pools (dedicated pools cannot route to shared-hosted). 3) Region selection uses a scored policy (latency penalty + capacity headroom + regulatory constraints) but must not violate active model pin region constraints. 4) Staged rollout weighting is applied only after candidates are filtered by pin/tier/region; canary cohorts are assigned using a sticky hash with expiration (default 1 hour) and an explicit cohort id stored in request metadata. 5) Fallbacks define capability-ordered variants; runtime prefers closest-capable variant in same region, else cross-region fallback respecting data residency. 6) When capacity or latency SLOs breach, routing should progressively degrade to the next variant and emit an event for observability and possible rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Routing resolver implements deterministic priority order: pin -> tier -> region scoring -> rollout weighting -> final variant selection
Canary cohort stickiness persists for 1 hour and honors cohort metadata across retries
Fallback chain preserves capability ordering and never routes to a variant lacking a required capability flag
Cross-region fallback requires explicit tenant consent unless data_residency==false
Integration tests covering: pin present but unavailable in region; canary cohort under capacity pressure; tier mismatch; fallback to quantized variant
Docs updated and sample routing configs added to console for rollout policies
tasks: Draft routing matrix and deterministic rulebook (this ticket)
Implement routing-resolver changes: scoring, cohort persistence, fallback lookup
Add unit tests for all matrix rows and edge cases
E2E test harness: simulate region outage and observe degrade paths
Console UI: surface chosen route + fallback reason for each request in traces
Create PR and run canary rollout in staging
tests: Unit: verify order of precedence for 120 unique input permutations
Integration: 3-region simulated deployment with one region saturated, validate cross-region fallback events
Load: sustained QPS with mixed pinned and unpinned requests to ensure routing latency < 5ms added overhead
Chaos: force model variant to crash, confirm routing quickly falls back and alerts are emitted
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature behind feature-flag. 2) Internal alpha to infra team for 48h traffic. 3) Stage canary: route 2% of production traffic with cohort sticky hash for 72h, monitor perf and output quality metrics. 4) Gradually increase to 25% over 3 days. 5) Full rollout after 7 days if no regressions. On rollback, revert feature flag and run automated rollback verification in staging before re-enabling.
observability: Emit a structured event for every routing decision containing: chosen_model_version, decision_path (list of rule hits as short codes), fallback_reason if any, cohort_id if applicable, latency_score, capacity_headroom, and tenant_tier. Create dashboard cards: routing-decision-distribution, fallback-rate-by-region, cohort-flap-rate. Alerts: fallback rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m and spike in cross-region routing.

notes: Edge case to decide: when an explicit pin points to a model version that exists only as a high-latency variant in the target region, should tiered tenants be allowed to opt-out automatically? Proposal: treat this as a soft warning and prefer a same-region lower-capability variant for P0 tenants only. Capture policy in policy table and revisit during design review.
